scriptural_facts.text: Lehi dwelt at Jerusalem all his days.
His sons called him a visionary man.

visual_design_choices: An Israelite man of Jerusalem, about sixty, around 600 BC.
Olive-brown skin, long grey-streaked beard, grey hair under a simple head covering, deep-set thoughtful eyes.
Ankle-length wool robe in natural cream with a brown striped mantle over the shoulders, leather belt, sandals.
Carries a wooden walking staff.
locked_traits: Same face, grey-streaked beard, and striped mantle in every panel.
Well-off but plain: no crown or royal regalia.

scriptural_facts.text: Sariah was Lehi's wife and the mother of Laman, Lemuel, Sam, and Nephi.

visual_design_choices: An Israelite woman of Jerusalem, in her sixties, around 600 BC.
Olive-brown skin, visibly aged and wrinkled, dark hair with a few grey strands, warm brown eyes, strong but kind features.
Long madder-red wool dress with an embroidered neckline, a cream linen head veil falling to her shoulders, simple bronze earrings.
locked_traits: Same face, madder-red dress, and cream veil in every panel.

scriptural_facts.text: Laman was Lehi's eldest son.
He murmured against his father.

visual_design_choices: An Israelite man in his late twenties, around 600 BC; the tallest and broadest of the brothers except Nephi.
Olive-brown skin, thick black beard, black hair to the jaw, heavy brow, a hard, resentful set to the mouth.
Dark ochre wool tunic, a fringed charcoal-brown mantle, wide leather belt with a dagger, sandals.
locked_traits: Same face, thick black beard, and ochre tunic in every panel.

scriptural_facts.text: Lemuel was Lehi's second son.
He murmured against his father with Laman.

visual_design_choices: An Israelite man in his mid twenties, around 600 BC; leaner than Laman.
Olive-brown skin, short black beard, black hair, narrow face, wary sidelong glance.
Olive-green wool tunic, a tan mantle, rope belt, sandals.
locked_traits: Same face, short beard, and olive-green tunic in every panel.

scriptural_facts.text: Sam was Lehi's third son.
Sam believed Nephi's words.

visual_design_choices: An Israelite young man about twenty, around 600 BC.
Olive-brown skin, light beard, curly dark-brown hair, open, earnest expression.
Undyed cream wool tunic, a sky-blue sash, a light brown mantle, sandals.
locked_traits: Same face, curly hair, and sky-blue sash in every panel.

scriptural_facts.text: Nephi was born of goodly parents and taught in the learning of his father.
Nephi was exceedingly young, yet large in stature.

visual_design_choices: An Israelite youth about 23, around 600 BC, already taller and broader than grown men. Very Muscular.
Olive-brown skin, a first thin beard along the jaw, shoulder-length dark-brown hair, steady determined eyes.
Cream linen tunic, a deep blue wool mantle, leather belt, sandals.
locked_traits: Same face, youthful build, and deep blue mantle in every panel.
Clearly the largest in stature among his brothers while clearly the youngest.

scriptural_facts.text: Laban kept the record of the Jews and a genealogy on plates of brass.
Laban was a mighty man who could command fifty.
His sword had a hilt of pure gold and a blade of most precious steel.
Laban wore armor.

visual_design_choices: A powerful Jerusalem official in his forties, around 600 BC, heavy-set and imposing.
Olive skin, oiled black beard, black hair bound with a gold band, proud heavy-lidded eyes.
Rich purple-and-crimson wool robe with gold embroidery, bronze scale armor over the chest, the gold-hilted sword at his belt.
locked_traits: Same face, oiled beard, and purple-and-crimson robe in every panel.
The gold-hilted, steel-bladed sword is always the same sword.

scriptural_facts.text: Zoram was the servant of Laban who had the keys of the treasury.

visual_design_choices: A Jerusalem household servant in his early twenties, around 600 BC.
Olive skin, clean-shaven, short black hair, alert, cautious eyes.
Plain grey-brown linen tunic, a leather cord at the waist hung with a ring of bronze keys, sandals.
locked_traits: Same face and ring of bronze keys in every panel before he joins Lehi's family.

scriptural_facts.text: Ishmael and his family lived at Jerusalem and went into the wilderness with Lehi's family.
His daughters married Lehi's sons and Zoram.

visual_design_choices: An elderly Israelite man of Jerusalem, around 600 BC, older than Lehi.
Weathered olive skin, long white beard, bald crown with white hair at the sides, gentle eyes.
Faded indigo wool robe, a cream mantle with tassels at the corners, walking staff, sandals.
locked_traits: Same face, white beard, and indigo robe in every panel.

scriptural_facts.text: He came with Jared and their families from the great tower when the language of the people was confounded.
The brother of Jared was a large and mighty man, highly favored of the Lord.

visual_design_choices: An ancient Mesopotamian man of the great-tower era, in his forties, far older in setting than Lehi's family.
Tall and massively built, deep bronze skin, long black beard in tight ringlets, black hair bound with a plain cord, intense dark eyes.
Long fringed wool wrap-garment in undyed tan and rust, draped over one shoulder, a wide woven belt, leather sandals.
No crown or royal ornament; a leader by bearing, not regalia.
locked_traits: Same face, ringleted black beard, and tan-and-rust fringed wrap in every panel.
Clearly larger and more powerfully built than the people around him.

scriptural_facts.text: Nephi taught his people to build buildings and to work in wood, iron, copper, brass, steel, gold, and silver.

visual_design_choices: The first generation in the promised land: Israelite-descended dress adapting to a new land.
Homespun wool and new cotton tunics in undyed cream and earth tones, simple mantles, leather belts, sandals.
Men mostly bearded; women with linen head coverings; practical craft tools and simple metal ornaments.
Skin tones vary naturally from person to person; skin color is never a group marker.
locked_traits: Plain, practical settler dress; still recognizably descended from Lehi's Jerusalem clothing.

scriptural_facts.text: They wandered the wilderness with a short skin girdle about their loins and their heads shaven; their skill was in the bow, the cimeter, and the ax.
They marked themselves with red in their foreheads.
Their heads were shorn, and they wore only a skin girded about their loins, with bows, arrows, stones, and slings.
They had no breastplates or shields.

visual_design_choices: Lean, hardened wilderness warriors of varied ages and builds.
Short animal-skin loin girdles, bare torsos, a red ochre mark on each forehead, shaven heads.
Carrying bows, quivers of arrows, slings, stones, curved cimeters, and axes.
Skin tones vary naturally from person to person; skin color is never a group marker.
locked_traits: Shaven heads, red forehead marks, skin girdles, and no armor, every time.

scriptural_facts.text: They came out from Jerusalem when Zedekiah was carried captive into Babylon and crossed the great waters.
They had many wars, brought no records, and their language had become corrupted.

visual_design_choices: Descendants of Jerusalem emigrants after centuries cut off from any records: Old World roots worn down into a rough local style.
Faded, much-mended wool and cotton garments in muted greens and browns, crude bronze ornaments, weathered leather.
Weapons carried casually from long habits of war: short swords, spears.
Skin tones vary naturally from person to person; skin color is never a group marker.
locked_traits: Visibly rougher and more worn than Mosiah's Nephites until the two peoples merge.

scriptural_facts.text: King Noah taxed the people a fifth of their gold, silver, ziff, copper, brass, iron, fatlings, and grain.
The high priests' seats were ornamented with pure gold.

visual_design_choices: Well-fed, indulgent court priests of varied ages.
Layered robes of rich dyed cotton in crimson, saffron, and deep green, heavy gold and copper collars, rings, and armbands.
Soft hands, no tools or weapons; an air of idle luxury.
Skin tones vary naturally from person to person; skin color is never a group marker.
locked_traits: Always the most extravagantly dressed people present, in clear contrast to Abinadi.

scriptural_facts.text: They marked themselves with red in their foreheads after the manner of the Lamanites, but had not shorn their heads.

visual_design_choices: Nephite dissenters: Nephite-style tunics and armor with a red forehead mark.
Full heads of hair, often tied back; the red mark is the one clear sign of their side.
Skin tones vary naturally from person to person; skin color is never a group marker.
locked_traits: Red forehead mark and unshorn hair, every time.

scriptural_facts.text: They buried their swords and all their weapons deep in the earth.

visual_design_choices: Converted Lamanite families, men, women, and elders, living peacefully.
Clean woven cotton tunics and wraps in soft blues and whites, simple shell and bead ornaments, full hair, no forehead marks.
No weapons of any kind.
Skin tones vary naturally from person to person; skin color is never a group marker.
locked_traits: Never armed; peaceful dress clearly distinct from Lamanite warriors.

scriptural_facts.text: They wore costly apparel, ringlets, bracelets, and ornaments of gold.

visual_design_choices: Proud, prosperous Nephite dissenters.
Fine dyed cotton robes in rich colors, hair in ringlets, gold bracelets, rings, and ornaments on every member.
Skin tones vary naturally from person to person; skin color is never a group marker.
locked_traits: Visibly wealthy and ornamented every time; ringlets and gold bracelets always present.

scriptural_facts.text: Moroni prepared his people with breastplates, arm-shields, shields to defend their heads, and thick clothing.

visual_design_choices: Disciplined Nephite soldiers of varied ages.
Thick quilted cotton armor, hardened breastplates, round arm-shields, and head shields; swords and spears.
Muted undyed and indigo cloth, uniform in cut.
Skin tones vary naturally from person to person; skin color is never a group marker.
locked_traits: Always armored with breastplate, arm-shield, and head shield, in clear contrast to unarmored Lamanite warriors.

scriptural_facts.text: There were two thousand young men who took up weapons of war to defend their country.
They were all young men, exceedingly valiant for courage, strength, and activity.

visual_design_choices: Youths in their late teens, lean and athletic, sons of the Anti-Nephi-Lehies.
Thick quilted cotton armor and head shields like the Nephite armies, with soft blue and white accents echoing their parents' dress.
Skin tones vary naturally from person to person; skin color is never a group marker.
locked_traits: Always visibly young; armored like Nephite soldiers.

scriptural_facts.text: They were girded after the manner of robbers, with a lamb-skin about their loins, dyed in blood, heads shorn, and head-plates upon them.

visual_design_choices: Menacing mountain bandits of varied ages and builds.
Lamb-skin loin coverings, shorn heads with dark metal head-plates.
'Dyed in blood' shown as dark rust-red dye streaked over skin and lamb-skins, never as wounds.
Skin tones vary naturally from person to person; skin color is never a group marker.
locked_traits: Lamb-skins, rust-red dye, shorn heads, and head-plates, every time.

visual_design_choices: An ancient New World civilization descended from the brother of Jared's people, far older than the Nephites.
Heavy woven wool and cotton garments in ochre, black, and deep red with bold geometric borders; large stone and obsidian ornaments; long braided hair.
Warriors carry broad swords and round shields; clearly not Nephite or Lamanite in style.
Skin tones vary naturally from person to person; skin color is never a group marker.
locked_traits: A distinct, older culture: never dressed like Nephites or Lamanites.

scriptural_facts.text: He descended out of heaven clothed in a white robe and stood in the midst of the multitude.

locked_traits: Only what scripture states: a man clothed in a white robe.
